chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman al-Minqari, from Fuzayl ibn Iyaz, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about certain things from the earnings (trade/commerce), so he forbade me from them, and said: 'O Fuzayl! By Allah! The harm of these (ruling authorities) upon this community is more severe than the harm of the Turks and the Daylam.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about abstention (war') from the people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who abstains from the prohibitions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and keeps away from these (ruling authorities).'
And when he does not guard against the doubtful matters, he falls into the forbidden (haram), and he does not recognize it.
And when he sees the evil so he does not deny it, whereas he is able to do so, then he loves to disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And the one who loves to disobey Allah, so he has duelled against Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with enmity.
And the one who loves the survival of the unjust ones, so he has loved to disobey Allah.
Indeed, Allah the Exalted praised Himself upon the destruction of the unjust ones, so He said:
So the roots of the people who were unjust were cut off; and all Praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true war' (abstention) according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines *war'* (piety) not merely as avoiding clear sins but as rigorous avoidance of *shubuhat* (doubtful matters) to prevent inadvertent transgression. He further links the passive acceptance of unjust rulers to active disobedience of Allah, citing the Quranic praise for the destruction of the unjust to underscore the spiritual danger of their persistence.
